biography: Andrew Hawkes, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in rallycross paddocks, hails from a small village nestled in the Cotswolds. His racing journey began, not on asphalt, but in muddy fields, tearing around on a battered quad bike his grandfather gifted him. That quad, and the freedom it represented, ignited a passion for speed and control that would define his life. He transitioned to karts at 16, showing flashes of brilliance, but an inconsistent temperament often saw him penalized for overly aggressive maneuvers. Rallycross offered a more suitable outlet for his raw talent. His defining moment came at Lydden Hill in 2018, where, despite starting last after a mechanical failure in qualifying, he clawed his way to victory, showcasing an almost preternatural ability to read the changing track conditions. Now at 36, Hawkes is considered to be in his prime but struggles to find consistency. His partnership with the Mini R60 RX team shows promise, but whether he can tame his inner demons and deliver on his potential remains to be seen. Some suspect that Andrew's inconsistent performance stems from the immense pressure he puts on himself, always striving for perfection, even if it means pushing beyond the limit.
drivingStyle: Hawkes' driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He attacks corners with an almost reckless abandon, often throwing the car into slides that seem impossible to recover from. His tire management is questionable, favoring short bursts of intense speed over consistent lap times. However, when the pressure is on, and the track conditions are treacherous, Hawkes possesses an uncanny ability to adapt and find grip where others cannot. He thrives on the chaos of rallycross, using his raw talent to overcome his tendency for over-aggression.

famousQuote: "Sometimes you gotta risk it for the biscuit. Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Lydden Hill Race after starting last, overcoming a mechanical failure and torrential rain to deliver a stunning performance.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the final race of the 2020 season while leading, costing him a chance at the championship title.
